questions.q: In what order does Theo cut traffic over to the three services on AKS, and why?
options: checkout-api first, since it's the most important
catalog-api first (lowest-risk, read-only), then cart-api, then checkout-api last, since every completed sale depends on it
All three at once, to save time
Alphabetical order
questions.explain: The parallel-path cutover goes from lowest-risk to highest-risk: catalog-api is read-only with no payment data, checkout-api is cut over last because it's the most consequential if something goes wrong.

questions.q: Why isn't 'the pods say Running' considered sufficient validation on its own?
options: Because kubectl often lies about pod status
Because it doesn't confirm the service's real endpoints respond correctly or that response shapes match the old infrastructure's contract
Because pods always say Running even when they've crashed
Because Running status only applies to checkout-api
questions.explain: Theo hits each service's real endpoints through the Ingress and confirms response shapes are unchanged, since Lesson 2 scoped this as a migration with no API contract changes allowed.

questions.q: What does `kubectl get pods -n storefront -o wide` actually tell you, and what does it NOT tell you?
options: It shows which availability zone each pod is in, and nothing else
It shows each pod's assigned node, but not which availability zone that node is in
It shows CPU usage per pod
It shows the Deployment's YAML definition
questions.explain: The NODE column shows which node a pod landed on; confirming multiple nodes are in use is not the same as confirming even distribution across availability zones.

questions.q: Why does today's spot-check of checkout-api's pod distribution look healthy, even though the anti-affinity gap from Lesson 4 is still unresolved?
options: Because the gap was actually fixed in this lesson
Because at today's normal, pre-sale baseline traffic, six replicas spread across nodes happen to cover more than one zone, which looks like a healthy, distributed picture
Because checkout-api doesn't use availability zones
Because the HPA has already scaled to 30 replicas
questions.explain: At low, normal traffic the pod count and placement look fine by chance; the gap only becomes visible under a fast scale-out with uneven real traffic, which this lesson doesn't test.

questions.q: What validation does this lesson explicitly NOT perform, and where is that validation deferred to?
options: Checking that pods are Running — deferred to Lesson 6
Confirming the cluster behaves correctly under sale-scale traffic and HPA scale-out — deferred to Lesson 8's load test and Lesson 9's actual sale
Checking API response shapes — deferred to Lesson 7
Nothing is deferred; this lesson is fully comprehensive
questions.explain: This lesson validates correct behavior after migration; validating behavior under sale-scale traffic and autoscaling is a distinct, harder question deferred to later lessons.
